analysis.investment_thesis: ASK Automotive earns excellent returns on capital (~28% ROIC/ROCE) but trades at a paltry 4.8% earnings yield (EBIT ₹432 Cr / EV ~₹9,003 Cr), making it expensive by Magic Formula standards. The business quality is real, but the price you pay today leaves little margin of safety.
key_strengths: High ROCE of 27.6% sustained and expanding — a genuinely good business
Revenue CAGR of 12.4% and net profit CAGR of 13.8% over 6 years show consistent compounding
Strong promoter holding (75%) and OEM-focused customer base provide stability
key_risks: Capex explosion (₹86 Cr → ₹346 Cr in 4 years) is crushing FCF to near-zero (₹30 Cr on ₹248 Cr net profit) — capital intensity is the enemy of Magic Formula returns
Borrowings nearly doubled in one year (₹346 → ₹612 Cr); rising debt is compressing financial flexibility
Auto components is a cyclical, low-moat OEM supplier — margin compression risk if OEM customers squeeze pricing
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~4.8% is well below my 6% minimum threshold — the stock is not cheap
FCF conversion is only 12% of net profit (₹30 Cr FCF vs ₹248 Cr net profit) — reported earnings are largely non-cash or being reinvested at scale
Borrowings surged 77% YoY (₹346 → ₹612 Cr) — balance sheet leverage accelerating rapidly
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT for FY2025 is ₹432 Cr. Enterprise Value = Market Cap (₹8,611 Cr) + Net Debt (₹412 Cr cash-adj to ~₹392 Cr) ≈ ₹9,003 Cr, giving an Earnings Yield of just 4.8% — far below my 6% floor and nowhere near the 12%+ that would excite me. The ROIC/ROCE story is better at 27.6%, clearing my 25% "excellent" bar, but when one leg of the Magic Formula is this weak, the combined ranking is mediocre at best. At EV/EBITDA of 18.8x and P/E of 30x, the market is fully pricing in the quality.

The deeper concern is capital intensity. ASK is in a massive capex cycle (₹346 Cr capex in FY2025 vs ₹360 Cr OCF), leaving free cash flow of a mere ₹30 Cr on ₹248 Cr of net profit — a 12% FCF conversion rate. This is not a cash-generative compounder right now; it is a heavy industrial build-out. If the new capacity (evidenced by ₹163 Cr CWIP) pays off, ROIC could sustain and debt could be serviced. But the Magic Formula rewards businesses that earn high returns on *existing* capital without needing continuous heavy reinvestment. Until the capex cycle normalizes and FCF conversion recovers to 60%+, the formula rank is impaired.
